components.title: The Water Cycle
components.subtitle: How water moves between the oceans, atmosphere, and land

components.text: The sun heats water in oceans, lakes, and rivers, turning it into water vapour that rises into the air. Plants also release water vapour through their leaves in a process called transpiration.
As warm, moist air rises, it cools. Cooler air holds less vapour, so the vapour condenses onto tiny particles of dust and salt, forming droplets that gather into clouds.
When cloud droplets grow heavy enough, they fall as rain, snow, sleet, or hail. The water then collects in oceans, lakes, rivers, and groundwater, and the cycle begins again.

components.label: WORKED EXAMPLE
components.title: A puddle disappears
components.body:
A 2-litre puddle sits on a sunny pavement. By afternoon it is gone. The sun heated the water, so it evaporated into the air as vapour.

Later, that vapour cools high in the atmosphere, condenses into a cloud, and may return as rain.
components.takeaway: Heat drives evaporation; vapour eventually returns to the ground as precipitation.

questions.question: What process turns liquid water into water vapour?
questions.explanation: Evaporation is caused by heat turning liquid water into vapour.

questions.question: What causes water vapour to form clouds?
questions.explanation: As air cools, it can hold less vapour, so the vapour condenses into droplets.

questions.question: Which of these is a form of precipitation?
questions.explanation: Snow is water falling from clouds, which makes it precipitation.
